A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SuperF research. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and match across the formatting changes; v2 adds a short Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution experiments on SatSynthBurst, SyntheticBurst and real satellite imagery, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The shared INR, directly parameterized alignment, supersampling, spectral projection and MSE/GNLL objectives remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies the existing RGB and uncertainty outputs without changing the architecture or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same satellite and handheld-image coverage: SatSynthBurst, SyntheticBurst, real Sentinel-2 examples and WorldStrat-sweet/bitter. The upsampling, large-shift and occlusion scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 retain bilinear interpolation, Lafenetre et al. (2023), and the adapted NIR baseline from Nam et al. (2022) at 2k and 5k iterations. Comparator participation and the other experimental comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3, Appendix A and Table 4 retain the same sample selections, resolutions, metrics, optimization budgets, boundary cropping, color matching and spatial alignment procedures. No evaluation setting is substantively revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Tables 2–3, frame-count and Fourier-scale analyses in Figures 6–8, large-shift tests in Table 6, and cloud-robustness analysis in Table 7 and Figure 10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same standard-deviation-across-samples reporting. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance procedures are added or revised. The clarified model-uncertainty description does not change statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–3 and 5–8 and the plotted and qualitative outcomes are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SatSynthBurst ×4 PSNR values of 32.94 for SuperF MSE and 34.03 for SuperF GNLL.

T1.justification: The image-formation assumptions, coordinate definitions, Equations (1)–(5), and Appendix A downsampling mathematics are retained. Explicitly identifying the uncertainty output in Section 3.3 explains existing mathematics rather than introducing a new definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about joint sub-pixel alignment, supersampling, SatSynthBurst, cross-domain applicability and avoiding high-resolution training data.

C2.justification: The explanations of alignment benefits, GNLL robustness and Fourier-scale sensitivity are unchanged. Both versions retain the runtime, changing-scene, overfitting and extreme-shift limitations in Section 4.6 and Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2's first-page footnote explicitly identifies code, dataset and demo availability at the existing project page; v1 only labels that link as the project page. New Appendix D discloses LLM assistance for literature research and coding. These are disclosure changes, not evidence of a new release or implementation.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. The Thera reference changes from an arXiv citation to its Transactions on Machine Learning Research publication, which is a bibliographic update rather than newly introduced related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical corrections and clarifies predictions versus targets in Section 3.2 and uncertainty outputs in Section 3.3. It adds the brief LLM-use appendix and refines cross-references and headings; the narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document-wide conversion to ICLR formatting changes margins, text width, title and author arrangement, headers, and figure/table sizing and placement. Figure 2 becomes substantially smaller, and Table 7 moves below Figure 9. All eight tables and thirteen figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 more clearly distinguish predictions, targets and uncertainty outputs, while the explicit resource statement and Appendix D improve transparency. These provide a modest overall gain. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the tighter conference layout makes some figures and tables smaller.
